data.name: Wizz by Virtuals
data.description:
Wizz started as a contributor network helping Web3 projects grow through bounties, content, research and distribution. Today, we're expanding that network into a data layer for AI Agents by transforming those internet signals into structured, developer-ready data.

Backed by 30,000+ users and 250+ partners, the network continuously generates real-world signals that power AI applications through DataCore.
data.tokenUtility:
$WIZZ is the native utility token used for: 

Projects: to create and fund bounty campaigns. Instead of paying contributors through multiple assets, projects can launch campaigns directly in $WIZZ, creating a unified reward system across the platform.

Contributors: Every contribution, whether it's content creation, research, education, design or community participation, will be rewarded in $WIZZ. 

Devs: access DataCore through API subscriptions, usage-based queries and future developer services. As more AI Agents integrate with Wizz, the token becomes the standard payment asset for accessing structured on-chain, social and web data.

Ecosystem: $WIZZ is also used to unlock premium platform features, participate in ecosystem incentive programs, receive holder benefits, and support future governance as the platform evolves.
data.roadmap:
Completed ( Q1 2025 - Q2 2026)

Built the Wizz bounty platform, enabling projects to launch campaigns and reward contributors.
Supported 100+ Web3 projects with community, education and content campaigns.
Built a community of 30,000+ users across the Wizz ecosystem.
Distributed $100K+  to thousands of contributors through completed bounty campaigns.

Next

Q3 2026: Token Generation Event (TGE) on Robinhood Chain via Virtuals, scheduled buy-and-burn program, holder distribution, wallet connect and verified account linking. 

Q4 2026: Launch of the first paid DataCore offering, on-chain bounty settlements, and portable on-chain contributor reputation. 

Q1 2027: Verifiable on-chain buybacks, DataCore subscription plans, per-query billing, holder fee discounts, and reward vesting. 

Q2 2027: Public DataCore API, recurring revenue reporting, staking for data providers, and community governance over data priorities and protocol fees.
data.additionalDetails:
Buyback & Burn Mechanism

During the first 13 months after launch, the protocol will buy back and burn $WIZZ on a published schedule, beginning with a higher burn rate during the initial launch period before transitioning to a steady monthly burn.

In addition to the scheduled programme, 25% of all protocol revenue is permanently burned. Since most revenue is collected in $WIZZ, these burns are primarily executed directly from protocol revenue and scale with platform usage.

data.name: Nakama Health by Virtuals
data.description: Traditional health insurance keeps plans, reserves, and decisions inside closed systems. Nakama is building the onchain health insurance layer: organizations launch tailored, funded plans; members claim privately; AI lowers operating costs; reserves and payouts are verifiable; and approved excess capital can earn yield. $NAKAMA coordinates the people, agents, and capital growing these plans into an open global insurance network.
data.tokenUtility:
$NAKAMA helps transform Nakama from a product operated by one company into an insurance network built and improved by many participants. It supports capital formation, network coordination, contributor incentives, and operator accountability.

Through ACF, part of the token supply is progressively converted into USDC as the project reaches higher valuations. This gives Nakama growth capital for product development, operations, ecosystem expansion, and sponsored health plans.

Holders can help shape policy standards, agent upgrades, grants, treasury priorities, and the direction of the network. Builders, researchers, operators, and other contributors can earn $NAKAMA for useful, verifiable work. As the network matures, qualified operators and evaluators can lock tokens behind their service commitments, creating a portable reputation and accountability layer for the people and agents running Nakama.
data.roadmap:
Day Zero puts the first Nakama health insurance layer onchain through Virtuals Protocol on Robinhood Chain. Nakama begins with trusted web3 teams and globally distributed communities because they already coordinate people and capital online and can adopt the model early.

During the first 90 days, Nakama will operate funded plans end to end, from enrollment and reserve management to claims, decisions, payments, and transparent reporting. ACF progressively converts part of the token allocation into USDC as the project grows, providing capital to improve the platform, expand operations, and sponsor new plans.

Next, Nakama will turn what works into reusable policies, software, APIs, and a network of qualified operators, evaluators, care partners, and capital providers. Licensed insurance and reinsurance partners will expand plan sizes, locations, and supported risks. Over time, regulated capital providers will be able to supply underwriting capacity and earn from premiums and reserve yield.

The destination is an open global market where organizations can launch programmable health insurance, members can carry protection across traditional boundaries, and capital can support health risk transparently onchain.
data.additionalDetails:
Nakama began with a question founder Marino Sabijan repeatedly encountered as a physician: why is financial help during a health crisis still difficult to understand, slow to arrive, and impossible to verify? He has spent two years turning that problem into a working product. Nakama’s earlier chapter reached more than 3,000 users, hundreds have joined the waitlist, and the core plan creation, member, agent, claims, and payment journeys are working.

Nakama’s main advantage is not simply putting insurance records onchain. It combines customizable plans, sponsored or shared funding, private claims, AI-assisted administration, transparent reserves, programmable payments, and productive capital in one system. This can lower operating costs, give organizations greater control, and make smaller or more specialized plans economically possible.

Nakama earns through plan launches, recurring administration, software, and agent operations. As the network matures, revenue can expand into licensed underwriting infrastructure, reserve management, reinsurance coordination, and capital-market services.

Robinhood Chain provides the open financial and RWA infrastructure for reserves, yield strategies, and programmable settlement. Virtuals provides tokenization, Automated Capital Formation, agent distribution, and ecosystem coordination. The planned one-billion-token supply allocates 50% to liquidity, 25% to ACF, and 25% to the vested team allocation.

Activate carefully tested HAN participation mechanics, Motion Credits, access controls, and contributor incentives only as the required contracts and anti-abuse systems become production-ready.

Extend the network across additional humanoid platforms, environments, and real-world task categories.

data.name: robinlaunchpad
data.description:
Count the apps holding your money right now.

The marketplace sitting on your NFT. The launchpad you aped into. A DEX with an LP position three tabs deep. A bridge still showing "pending" from Tuesday. Each took custody somewhere, and each has a withdraw button you're trusting a stranger to honor. That's the real tax on being onchain. Not gas. Custody.

RobinLaunchpad's whole argument: the number should be one, and the custodian should be nobody.

It's live at robinlaunchpad.com, on Robinhood Chain — an Arbitrum L2, chainId 4663, where native ETH is both the gas and the money you trade with. No wrapped stand-in to buy first. Desktop and mobile wallets, a 3D "onchain void," ⌘K to jump anywhere. The UI's the fun part, not the thesis. The thesis is one load-bearing phrase: approval, not custody. You sign; the platform never holds your funds.

The NFT marketplace is where that gets tested. List at a fixed price and the NFT never leaves your wallet — the buyer pulls it the second they pay, and that's the only power the contract has. Offers and bids are the exception, because a bid nobody can enforce is just a tweet, so those get escrowed. Auctions run English with anti-snipe: bid in the final seconds and the clock adds ten minutes, so you win by bidding more, not by refreshing faster. Royalties are EIP-2981 up to 10%, auto-split at settlement. Floor sweep clears the bottom shelf in one tx.

Inscriptions use the chain as storage. You write data straight into a transaction as calldata — a data: URI that lives there forever — and it comes back stamped with a sequential ordinal number. Text, images, JSON. Sell a 1/1 through an escrow market that holds it only while it's listed; delist and it's home the same block. No server to go dark on you. There isn't one.

rh-20 stacks a fungible standard on that, BRC-20 in spirit, and the rule that matters is fair launch by construction: no presale, no team bag. Deploy a ticker, mints go first-come-first-served, and you can't sell until it's fully minted out — the deployer crosses the line with everyone else. NFT Drops aim the same discipline at creators: an ERC-721 with a paid public mint in one tx, you set price, supply, per-wallet cap and royalty, you own the contract, proceeds land instantly, overpay refunds itself, no trading until it's 100% minted.

The memecoin launchpad is the pump.fun shape. A token trades the instant it exists with zero seed liquidity, because price runs off a constant-product bonding curve, not a pool someone had to fund. Every buy walks it up. Dev-buy in the launch tx and snipers eat your dust. Creator takes 1% of every trade. At 80% bought it graduates: leftover tokens plus all raised ETH lock into a pool for good — keeps trading, nobody can pull it. There's a shareable PnL card whose art shifts by tier. Mooning, in profit, rekt. Same button for bragging and coping.

Liquidity & Pools is where non-custodial turns into math. A live, auto-detected map of every V2 and V3 pair. Add or remove from the UI, signing each move. V2 fees auto-compound; V3 concentrates a range and shows the exact claimable fees plus whether you're in range or just cosplaying an LP. Swap fees go 100% to LPs, no skim. LP PnL is the honest kind, rebuilt from onchain history with impermanent loss counted, in ETH — and it all rolls into one portfolio, memecoins and NFTs and inscriptions and LP, with allocation and all-time PnL.

The Bridge does a bridge's one job: LI.FI routing through audited bridges from Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BSC and more into RH Chain. RobinLaunchpad hosts the interface. That's it.

Trading Agents are in beta, and the honest version is short: bring your own AI key, agents pitch trades in character — Degen, Sniper, LP Farmer, ten providers — and they recommend, full stop. Your wallet signs, the key never leaves your browser. Worst case, one talks you into a trade you'd have found by 3am anyway.

Notice what none of it does. The marketplace won't hold your NFT. The launchpads won't sit on the mint. The bridge won't hold your bridge. The agents won't hold your keys. The graduated pool is locked so tight the founders can't reach in. No withdraw button anywhere, because there's nothing to withdraw from. The money was never anywhere but your own wallet.

Go poke at it: robinlaunchpad.com. And @robinlaunchpad if you feel like yelling at us.
